Fetch Data using API¶

In [11]:
import requests
import time
import numpy as np
In [12]:
TMDB_API_KEY = 'c94ff70353a867587e0ee7464a4b2e19'
In [13]:
BASE_URL = 'https://api.themoviedb.org/3/movie/{}/credits?api_key=' + TMDB_API_KEY
In [14]:
movieID = horror['movieId'].tolist()
tmdbID = horror['tmdbId'].tolist()

directors = []
all_cast = []
stored_movieIDs = []
In [15]:
for i, tmdb_ID in enumerate(tmdbID):
    if pd.notna(tmdb_ID):
        url = BASE_URL.format(int(tmdb_ID))
        try:
            response = requests.get(url)
            response.raise_for_status()
            data = response.json()
            director = next(
                (crew_member['name'] for crew_member in data.get('crew', []) 
                 if crew_member.get('job') == 'Director'),
                np.nan 
            )
            cast = [cast_member['name'] for cast_member in data.get('cast', [])[:5]]
            top_cast = ', '.join(cast) if cast else np.nan
            directors.append(director)
            all_cast.append(top_cast)
            stored_movieIDs.append(movieID[i])
            
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
            print(f"Request Error for TMDB ID {tmdb_ID}: {e}")
            directors.append(np.nan)
            all_cast.append(np.nan)
            stored_movieIDs.append(movieID[i])
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Processing Error for TMDB ID {tmdb_ID}: {e}")
            directors.append(np.nan)
            all_cast.append(np.nan)
            stored_movieIDs.append(movieID[i])
            
    time.sleep(0.1) 
    
print("API call loop complete.")

Merge Ratings¶

In [20]:
rating_stats = ratings.groupby('movieId').agg(
    avg_rating = ('rating', 'mean'),      
    count_rating = ('rating', 'count')    
).reset_index()

horror = pd.merge(horror, rating_stats, on='movieId', how='inner')

horror['rating_count_log'] = np.log1p(horror['count_rating'])

print(f"Rating features added. Current shape of 'horror': {horror.shape}")

Merge Tags¶

In [22]:
movie_tags = pd.merge(
    tags[['movieId', 'tag']],
    horror[['movieId', 'is_black_centered']], 
    on='movieId',
    how='inner'
)

all_tags = movie_tags.groupby('movieId')['tag'].apply(
    lambda x: ' '.join(x.astype(str).str.lower())
).reset_index(name='all_tags')


horror = pd.merge(
    horror, 
    all_tags, 
    on='movieId', 
    how='inner'
)

print(f"'all_tags' created and merged into the full dataset.")
print(f"Final dataset size: {horror.shape[0]} movies.")

'all_tags' created and merged into the full dataset.

horror['all_tags'].fillna('', inplace=True) #replacing missing tags with an empty string

vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(stop_words='english', max_features=500, min_df=5)
#picks the 500 most important words (max_features=500; min_df=5 ingnores words that appear less than 5 times)

X_tags = vectorizer.fit_transform(horror['all_tags']) #where vectorizer gets words from

X_tags_df = pd.DataFrame(X_tags.toarray(), 
                         columns=vectorizer.get_feature_names_out()) #dataframe for the 500 words

y = horror['is_black_centered'].reset_index(drop=True) 

X_ratings = horror[['avg_rating', 'rating_count_log']] #dataframe for ratings; rating_count_log represents total number of users who rated a film

X_full = pd.concat([X_tags_df, X_ratings.reset_index(drop=True)], axis=1) #joins ratings and tags

print(f"{X_tags.shape[1]} tag features. {X_ratings.shape[1]} rating features.")
print(f"Shape: {X_full.shape}")

feature_names = np.array(X_train_tags.columns)
log_prob_0 = clf.feature_log_prob_[0] 
log_prob_1 = clf.feature_log_prob_[1]

log_ratio = log_prob_1 - log_prob_0 #difference in log probabilities. high value => black horror

feature_importance = pd.DataFrame({
    'word': feature_names,
    'log_ratio': log_ratio
}).sort_values(by='log_ratio', ascending=False)

print("\n--- Top Tags BLACK horror ---")
print(feature_importance.head(10).to_markdown(index=False))

print("\n--- Top Tags GENERAL Horror ---")
print(feature_importance.tail(10).to_markdown(index=False))

print("Model training complete.")

rating_count_log - Most Important Feature: This feature alone was responsible for ~11.3% of the Random Forest model's predictive power. It suggests that the popularity/exposure of a film is the single best way to separate the two classes (likely because Black-Centered films tend to have lower exposure).

avg_rating - Second Most Important: This feature accounted for ~11.0% of the predictive power.

horror - Most Important Tag: This common tag was responsible for ~3.1% of the predictive power.

All other tags < 0.025 The remaining tags each contributed a small amount to the overall prediction.

Visualizations¶

Naive Bayes¶

In [73]:
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

def plot_decision_boundary(X, y, classifier, title, ax):
    """Plots the decision boundary for a classifier trained on 2D data."""
    h = 0.02 
    x_min, x_max = X[:, 0].min() - 0.5, X[:, 0].max() + 0.5
    y_min, y_max = X[:, 1].min() - 0.5, X[:, 1].max() + 0.5
    xx, yy = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x_min, x_max, h),
                         np.arange(y_min, y_max, h))
    Z = classifier.predict(np.c_[xx.ravel(), yy.ravel()])
    Z = Z.reshape(xx.shape)
    
    ax.contourf(xx, yy, Z, alpha=0.8, cmap=plt.cm.coolwarm)
    scatter = ax.scatter(X[:, 0], X[:, 1], c=y, edgecolors='k', s=50, 
                         marker='o', cmap=plt.cm.coolwarm)
    
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14)
    ax.set_xlabel('Principal Component 1', fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel('Principal Component 2', fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(scatter.legend_elements()[0], ['General Horror (0)', 'Black Horror (1)'], 
              title="True Class", loc='lower right', fontsize=8)

pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_full) 
X_train_pca, X_test_pca, y_train_pca, y_test_pca = train_test_split(
    X_pca, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))

X_train_pca_nb = np.maximum(X_train_pca, 0) 
nb_pca = MultinomialNB()
nb_pca.fit(X_train_pca_nb, y_train_pca)

plot_decision_boundary(X_test_pca, y_test_pca, nb_pca, 
                       "Naive Bayes", ax)

plt.suptitle('Naive Bayes Decision Boundary on PCA Data', fontsize=16)
plt.show()
print("Naive Bayes plot displayed.")

Naive Bayes plot displayed.
